nodes.question: What did the recent study on gaur and sambar in central India focus on?
nodes.answer: The study focused on how landscape genetics provide insights into the effects of landscape structure permeability and gene flow on large-bodied herbivores.
nodes.paragraph: For example, a recent study on the herbivorous gaur (Bos gaurus) and sambar (Rusa unicolor) in central India, demonstrated that landscape genetics can pro- vide insights into effects of landscape structure per - meability, and subsequent gene flow, on large-bodied herbivores (Tyagi et al. 2024). The study revealed that land-use changes had a more pronounced effect on gaur connectivity, while roads and human population density more significantly affected sambar connectiv - ity. Understanding spatio-genetic barriers is integral to effective conservation strategies that enhance gene flow and mitigate loss of genetic diversity. However, research in this space has predominately centred Landsc Ecol (2025) 40:58 58 Vol. : (123456789) around threatened species and species of carnivorous diets (Thatte et al. 2020; Fusco et al. 2021). This nar - row focus has created a substantial gap in our under - standing of species that are considered of least con- cern but are ecologically and culturally significant, such as woodland-dwelling organisms (Lino et al. 2019).
